passage: When I was nine, my mother let me carry a steel plate of Diwali laddoos to the neighbours. My favourite door was Seema Aunty's. She always said, "Wait, wait, don't go," and came back with a small bowl of something. That evening it was kheer. In the summer she had sent sewaiyan to us for Eid, and I had carried back a bowl of our sweet rice. I remember walking home slowly with the warm bowl, thinking that food goes both ways on our floor. That night I could smell sugar and cardamom from three different kitchens. It felt as if the whole building was having one big party. Jagdish

qa.q: What did Seema Aunty give Jagdish that evening?
qa.a: Seema Aunty gave Jagdish a small bowl of kheer.

qa.q: How did Jagdish feel walking home with the warm bowl?
qa.a: Jagdish felt happy and connected, as if the whole building was having one big party. 😊

qa.q: Which small gesture made the festival feel bigger than one home?
qa.a: Carrying sweets to the neighbours and getting bowls back, so that food went both ways on their floor.

qa.q: How might Seema Aunty have felt when Jagdish arrived with laddoos?
qa.a: Glad and warm. She said "Wait, wait, don't go" and came back with a bowl to share, which shows she enjoyed the exchange.

grounding: A child shares festival food with neighbours and feels part of something bigger than one home.

passage: Note to parents, Class 4, after the Eid weekend. Tanvir, 9, arrived on Monday with a tiffin of sewaiyan and a paper bag of small bowls. He said, "Ammi made lots so I can give one to everybody." He went round the class and gave each child a bowl, including Joseph and Kavya, who had shared their Christmas and Diwali sweets with him earlier. He gave the last bowl to the school guard, who smiled and said, "Eid Mubarak, beta." Tanvir looked proud all morning. I asked why he shared so much. He said, "Because then everyone is in Eid." I have thanked his mother and will invite all children to describe a festival at home next week. Ramesh, class teacher 🙂

qa.q: What did Tanvir bring to school on Monday?
qa.a: Tanvir brought a tiffin of sewaiyan and a paper bag of small bowls.

qa.q: What was Tanvir feeling as he gave out the bowls?
qa.a: Tanvir was proud and happy, wanting everyone to be part of Eid, as he said: "Then everyone is in Eid."

qa.q: What choice did Ramesh make after seeing Tanvir share?
qa.a: Ramesh thanked Tanvir's mother and planned to invite all the children to describe a festival at home, so the sharing could continue.

qa.q: How might the school guard have felt receiving the last bowl?
qa.a: Pleased and included, since the guard smiled and said "Eid Mubarak, beta."

grounding: A child shares Eid sweets with classmates and others and feels part of something bigger than one home.
